tools.name: adversarial_check
tools.description:
Requires the Stochastly desktop app: this tool runs inside the app, which is not installed on this machine. Install it from https://stochastly.com/pricing, open it and activate a licence.

Run six controls that try to refute a finished run (drift against its own block-bootstrap
null, an edge-free twin of the prop-firm cycle, Romano-Wolf multiplicity, concentration on the
best days, frictions, stability across sub-periods) plus a positive control that checks a
known edge would be detected on the same data.

Call it after any promising result. `synthesis` is SURVIVES, REFUTED, UNDERPOWERED (effect
smaller than the sample can resolve; `observations_needed` says how many bars it would take)
or BLIND (the positive control failed, so the sample, not the strategy, must change). Each
passed control reports its `floor`, the smallest effect it could have rejected. Deterministic
arithmetic, no language model; measured error rates in the test suite: 0.017 false
positives, 0.000 false negatives. Needs the run's full PnL series with at least 8 points; an
unknown run is a named error. Needs Stochastly open with an Atelier or Portfolio licence.

run_id.description: Id of a finished run, from backtest_graph or backtest_status.
run_id.title: Run Id

n_sims.description: Number of simulations for the randomised controls.
n_sims.title: N Sims

seed.description: Random seed; the same seed gives the same answer.
seed.title: Seed

annotations.title: Try to refute a finished run

tools.name: analyze_dependence
tools.description:
Requires the Stochastly desktop app: this tool runs inside the app, which is not installed on this machine. Install it from https://stochastly.com/pricing, open it and activate a licence.

Measure the dependence between two equity curves you supply, by fitting one copula or the
mutual information to their paired increments (only timestamps present in both curves count).

Use it to ask whether two strategies or markets move together before combining them; to
actually build and judge a combined book from finished runs, use portfolio_combine instead.
Descriptive only: it reports the fit, it does not run a hypothesis test or take a decision.
Malformed curves are refused with a named error (wrong count, missing unit, unordered dates,
non-finite values). Needs Stochastly open with an Atelier or Portfolio licence.

instruments.description: Exactly two curves. Each is an object with `equity` (list of finite numbers, at least 2), an optional `symbol`, `timestamps` or `dates` (ISO dates, same length, unique, increasing) and `pnl_unit` set to "R" or "return".
instruments.title: Instruments

kind.description: Dependence model: a gaussian, student, clayton or gumbel copula fit, or mutual_information on the ranks.
kind.title: Kind

tools.name: app_info
tools.description:
Requires the Stochastly desktop app: this tool runs inside the app, which is not installed on this machine. Install it from https://stochastly.com/pricing, open it and activate a licence.

Report the installed Stochastly app: version, build_edition, platform, python, cpu_count,
hw_factor, license_status (key masked), build (git commit, dirty flag, engine fingerprint),
engine_integrity (whether the running engine matches that fingerprint) and `_engine`
(`sidecar` when it talks to the open app, `in-process` in a source checkout).

Call it first to check that the app is reachable and which plan is active; a refusal from any
other tool names the plan it needs. Needs Stochastly open with an Atelier or Portfolio licence.

tools.name: backtest_graph
tools.description:
Requires the Stochastly desktop app: this tool runs inside the app, which is not installed on this machine. Install it from https://stochastly.com/pricing, open it and activate a licence.

Run a strategy graph end to end on your data: build the configurations, run a cost-aware
backtest with leakage-free splits, apply the overfitting gates and return the verdict, the
number of survivors and the run_id. Each finished run is added to the day's session registry,
and `multiplicity` reports how many runs and configurations this session has tried.

Check the plan with compose_graph first. Data comes from `data_root` or a registered
`source`; nothing is downloaded for you and an unknown source is refused. A plan with custom
Python is refused unless the user allowed custom code on this machine. Use background=true for
long runs, then backtest_status. Requires an Atelier or Portfolio licence.

plan.description: Strategy graph, same shape as in compose_graph; node keys come from node_catalog.
plan.title: Plan

source.description: Registered data source name from data_sources; "folder" reads data_root. An existing folder path given here is used as data_root.
source.title: Source

symbols.description: Symbols to trade; omit for the default universe, which the run names in its note.
symbols.title: Symbols

cap.description: Maximum number of parameter configurations evaluated.
cap.title: Cap

timeout_s.description: Seconds to wait for the result (minimum 5); after that, poll backtest_status.
timeout_s.title: Timeout S

data_root.description: Folder holding your own price files.
data_root.title: Data Root

background.description: True returns a run_id at once; poll backtest_status for the result.
background.title: Background

tools.name: backtest_status
tools.description:
Requires the Stochastly desktop app: this tool runs inside the app, which is not installed on this machine. Install it from https://stochastly.com/pricing, open it and activate a licence.

Get the state of a graph run started by backtest_graph: while running, status, progress and
message; once done, failed or cancelled, the same summary backtest_graph returns (verdict,
survivors, multiplicity).

Use it after backtest_graph with background=true, or when a foreground run hit its timeout.
A finished run is recorded once in the day's session registry. An unknown run_id is a named
error. Needs Stochastly open with an Atelier or Portfolio licence.

tools.name: compose_graph
tools.description:
Requires the Stochastly desktop app: this tool runs inside the app, which is not installed on this machine. Install it from https://stochastly.com/pricing, open it and activate a licence.

Check a strategy graph plan and turn it into a run specification, counting how many
parameter configurations it would test. Nothing is executed and no data is read.

Use it to build and debug a plan before backtest_graph, which takes the same arguments.
Returns ok, configs, runnable, strategy, filters, gates and the full spec; an invalid plan
returns ok false with the exact field at fault. A plan carrying custom Python is reported in
`custom_code_nodes` with `runnable_over_mcp`, since backtest_graph refuses it unless the user
allowed custom code. Strategy and filter params are single-value locks; omit one to sweep its
catalogue values. Gates take a threshold, op "ge" or "le", and window "oos", "is", "oos2",
"sealed", "full" or "wfa". Cost nodes charge the run; lectures are informational. Needs
Stochastly open with an Atelier or Portfolio licence.

plan.description: Strategy graph. Keys: strategy {key, params, code}, filters [{key, params, code, mode}], gates [{key, threshold, params, op, window}], lectures [{key, params}], execution {..}, data {is_pct, oos1_pct, purge_bars, embargo_bars, wfa_is_len, wfa_oos_len}, cost, cost_nodes [{name, params}], propfirm, propfirm_ev. Node keys are "family/name" from node_catalog.
plan.title: Plan

direction.description: Trade direction: "L" (long only), "S" (short only) or "LS" (both); long, short, both and similar spellings are accepted.
direction.title: Direction

symbols.description: Symbols to trade; omit for the default universe.
symbols.title: Symbols

tools.name: crypto_registry
tools.description:
Requires the Stochastly desktop app: this tool runs inside the app, which is not installed on this machine. Install it from https://stochastly.com/pricing, open it and activate a licence.

List the cross-sectional crypto strategies (momentum and mean reversion) with their
timeframes, directions, parameter grids and filters; each entry carries an `implemented` flag.

Use it to see which crypto ranking strategies exist. For graph node keys use node_catalog;
for the general strategy families use registries. Needs Stochastly open with an Atelier or
Portfolio licence.

tools.name: data_sources
tools.description:
Requires the Stochastly desktop app: this tool runs inside the app, which is not installed on this machine. Install it from https://stochastly.com/pricing, open it and activate a licence.

List the data source names registered in this build, as `sources`; "folder" (a folder of
your own price files) is always one of them.

Use it before backtest_graph to pick its `source` argument. A source missing from this list
is not available: pass `data_root` (a folder of price files) to backtest_graph instead.
Needs Stochastly open with an Atelier or Portfolio licence.

tools.name: diagnostic_explain
tools.description:
Requires the Stochastly desktop app: this tool runs inside the app, which is not installed on this machine. Install it from https://stochastly.com/pricing, open it and activate a licence.

Explain one diagnostic code: what the quantity measures, why it matters, and which
measurement could move the verdict (never a promise that an action will improve it).

Use it on codes returned by red_flag_check; list every code with diagnostics_catalog. An
unknown code returns an error with the list of known codes. Needs Stochastly open with an
Atelier or Portfolio licence.

code.description: Diagnostic code such as "OF01", "OF03" or "CO01", as returned in red_flag_check `violations`.
code.title: Code

tools.name: diagnostics_catalog
tools.description:
Requires the Stochastly desktop app: this tool runs inside the app, which is not installed on this machine. Install it from https://stochastly.com/pricing, open it and activate a licence.

List every diagnostic code the app can raise, as `diagnostics` (code, family, page) and
`severities`.

Use it to know what the checks can hold against a run, and so what they cannot judge yet;
explain one code with diagnostic_explain. Needs Stochastly open with an Atelier or Portfolio
licence.

tools.name: export_atlas
tools.description:
Requires the Stochastly desktop app: this tool runs inside the app, which is not installed on this machine. Install it from https://stochastly.com/pricing, open it and activate a licence.

Write one research paper PDF per finished run with a shared layout and title, and return
ok, dir, n, papers ({name, path, pages, rank, or error} each) and failed.

Use it to report several runs consistently; export_paper handles a single run. Every paper
prints how many papers the batch contains, because producing N reports is N trials. Every
run must be finished and carry a verdict, otherwise nothing is written; a paper that fails
to render is listed with its error. Requires an Atelier or Portfolio licence.

run_ids.description: Ids of the finished runs, one paper each.
run_ids.title: Run Ids

out_dir.description: Output folder; files with the same names are overwritten. Omit for a new folder in the app's papers folder.
out_dir.title: Out Dir

layout.description: Ordered section ids from paper_sections, shared by every paper.
layout.title: Layout

tools.name: export_paper
tools.description:
Requires the Stochastly desktop app: this tool runs inside the app, which is not installed on this machine. Install it from https://stochastly.com/pricing, open it and activate a licence.

Write a multi-page research paper PDF for one finished backtest run: abstract, numbered
equations, tables, robustness section and a mandatory backtest disclosures box. Returns ok,
path, pages, figures, tables, omitted and the layout actually printed.

Use it for a full write-up of one run; export_tearsheet makes a one-page summary and
export_atlas a batch of papers. Every number comes from the run; a section whose data the run
lacks is omitted with a note, and an unknown layout id is an error. Requires an Atelier or
Portfolio licence.

run_id.description: Id of a finished backtest run.
run_id.title: Run Id

path.description: Output PDF path; an existing file there is overwritten. Omit for a new time-stamped file in the app's results folder.
path.title: Path

hypothesis.description: The hypothesis registered before the search. Only pass it if that is true; without it the paper is labelled exploratory.
hypothesis.title: Hypothesis

instrument.description: Instrument name printed on the paper.
instrument.title: Instrument

layout.description: Ordered section ids from paper_sections; omit for the default paper.
layout.title: Layout

tools.name: export_tearsheet
tools.description:
Requires the Stochastly desktop app: this tool runs inside the app, which is not installed on this machine. Install it from https://stochastly.com/pricing, open it and activate a licence.

Write a one-page tearsheet image or PDF summarising a finished run, and return ok, path and
fmt.

Use it for a quick shareable summary; export_paper writes the full paper. Research runs have
no tearsheet and are refused, as are unknown or unfinished runs. Requires an Atelier or
Portfolio licence.

run_id.description: Id of a finished backtest, ML or portfolio run.
run_id.title: Run Id

fmt.description: "png" or "pdf"; any other value gives png.
fmt.title: Fmt

path.description: Output file path; an existing file there is overwritten. Omit for tearsheet_<run_id> in the app's tearsheets folder.
path.title: Path

tools.name: live_state
tools.description:
Requires the Stochastly desktop app: this tool runs inside the app, which is not installed on this machine. Install it from https://stochastly.com/pricing, open it and activate a licence.

Read what the open app last reported it is showing (workspace, chart, symbol, timeframe,
indicators, graph nodes, current run, active assistant agent; never secrets) from its state
file, with `age_s` (seconds since it was written) and `present` (false when the app has never
written it).

Use it to check the effect of pilot_app or the context of the user's screen. A large age_s
means the app is probably closed. Needs Stochastly open with an Atelier or Portfolio licence.

tools.name: node_catalog
tools.description:
Requires the Stochastly desktop app: this tool runs inside the app, which is not installed on this machine. Install it from https://stochastly.com/pricing, open it and activate a licence.

Return the graph editor's node catalogue, grouped by family: every strategy, filter, gate,
cost and reading node with its parameter schema, plus an `exportable` flag on strategies.

This is the only source of valid node keys ("family/name") for compose_graph and
backtest_graph; call it before writing a plan. Needs Stochastly open with an Atelier or
Portfolio licence.

force.description: True reloads the catalogue from the engine instead of the in-memory copy; only needed after the engine was updated while the app was open.
force.title: Force

tools.name: paper_sections
tools.description:
Requires the Stochastly desktop app: this tool runs inside the app, which is not installed on this machine. Install it from https://stochastly.com/pricing, open it and activate a licence.

List every section a research paper can contain, each as {id, group, label, mandatory,
in_default}, default sections first in print order.

Use it to choose the `layout` ids for export_paper or export_atlas. Mandatory sections (the
simulation letterhead and the backtest disclosures) are always added back, and the paper
follows the order you pass. Needs Stochastly open with an Atelier or Portfolio licence.

tools.name: pilot_app
tools.description:
Requires the Stochastly desktop app: this tool runs inside the app, which is not installed on this machine. Install it from https://stochastly.com/pricing, open it and activate a licence.

Drive the open Stochastly app on the user's screen: open a .stly document, switch screen,
show a chart, start a backtest, display a note or send a prompt to the in-app assistant.
Fields combine in one call and apply in the order open, screen, chart, run; the user sees
each step in the status bar and the session journal.

Use it when the user should watch the work in the app; to run a graph and get its numbers
back directly, use backtest_graph. The command replaces any pending one. It has no effect
unless the app is open and the user enabled piloting (off by default); the response always
carries `pilot_enabled`. Requires an Atelier or Portfolio licence.

session_path.description: Path to a .stly document (at most 8 MB) to open in the Build screen. Only a summary of it comes back, never its content.
session_path.title: Session Path

workspace.description: Screen to switch to: Home, Build, Backtest, Analyze, Results or Research.
workspace.title: Workspace

run.description: True starts a backtest on the graph in place. Cannot be combined with prompt. Refused for a document with custom Python unless the user allowed it.
run.title: Run

chart.description: Chart key to show in the display panel.
chart.title: Chart

note.description: Message shown to the user on screen; say what you are doing and why.
note.title: Note

sym.description: Legacy symbol field, ignored by the current app.
sym.title: Sym

tf.description: Legacy timeframe field, ignored by the current app.
tf.title: Tf

prompt.description: Text for the in-app assistant, or a command: /verdict <hypothesis>, /research [@agent...] [rounds=N] [budget=N] <topic>, /stop. Cannot be combined with run.
prompt.title: Prompt

tools.name: portfolio_combine
tools.description:
Requires the Stochastly desktop app: this tool runs inside the app, which is not installed on this machine. Install it from https://stochastly.com/pricing, open it and activate a licence.

Combine several finished runs into one portfolio (book) and judge it: returns the combined
series, the weights actually used, the correlation matrix between sleeves, each sleeve's
contribution and a deflated Sharpe ratio. The book is saved as a new run, so
adversarial_check and export_tearsheet accept its run_id.

Use it for a multi-strategy or multi-market book; a single graph run covers one strategy, and
analyze_dependence only measures two curves you supply. Weights at bar t use only bars before
t, and the drawdown cap acts on the previous bar's equity. Nothing is re-simulated: runs must
be finished in the current app session; runs in different PnL units are refused, not
converted. Requires a Portfolio licence (Atelier gets a named refusal).

run_ids.description: Comma-separated ids of at least 2 finished runs from this app session (a unique prefix is enough).
run_ids.title: Run Ids

method.description: Weighting: equal weights, volatility targeting, risk parity, or hierarchical risk parity.
method.title: Method

lookback.description: Trailing window in bars used to estimate weights.
lookback.title: Lookback

vol_target.description: Target volatility per bar for the whole book; 0 turns it off.
vol_target.title: Vol Target

max_leverage.description: Upper bound on the book's leverage.
max_leverage.title: Max Leverage

dd_cap.description: Drawdown at which the book is de-levered; 0 turns it off.
dd_cap.title: Dd Cap

dd_derisk.description: Leverage multiplier applied once dd_cap is reached.
dd_derisk.title: Dd Derisk

n_trials.description: Number of candidate sleeves to deflate the Sharpe ratio by; 0 uses the number of runs passed.
n_trials.title: N Trials

tools.name: reality_check_profiles
tools.description:
Requires the Stochastly desktop app: this tool runs inside the app, which is not installed on this machine. Install it from https://stochastly.com/pricing, open it and activate a licence.

Return the three synthetic example profiles of the reality check screen (profitable,
marginal, overfit) and the prop-firm rule presets it can apply (FTMO Standard and Pro 100k
phase 1, The5ers Hyper Growth).

Reference data only: to judge a real result use red_flag_check or adversarial_check. Needs
Stochastly open with an Atelier or Portfolio licence.

tools.name: red_flag_check
tools.description:
Requires the Stochastly desktop app: this tool runs inside the app, which is not installed on this machine. Install it from https://stochastly.com/pricing, open it and activate a licence.

Combine five overfitting measures into one deployment verdict, GREEN, AMBER or RED, with a
score from 0 (no red flag) to 100 (severe); RED sets `deploy_blocked`. Also returns each component and its contribution,
reasons, `violations` (diagnostic codes with severity), which measures were missing, and the
coverage needed for GREEN.

Use it to decide whether a configuration or run is fit to deploy. Pass null for anything you
did not measure: missing evidence lowers coverage instead of being guessed. Explain a code
from `violations` with diagnostic_explain; to try to refute a finished run, use
adversarial_check. Needs Stochastly open with an Atelier or Portfolio licence.

selection_score.description: Multiple-testing adjusted p-value (Romano-Wolf) returned by every run in `selection.score`; lower is better. null if not measured.
selection_score.title: Selection Score

dsr.description: Deflated Sharpe ratio of the result; null if not measured.
dsr.title: Dsr

oos_is_sharpe_ratio.description: Out-of-sample Sharpe divided by in-sample Sharpe; null if not measured.
oos_is_sharpe_ratio.title: Oos Is Sharpe Ratio

realization_ratio.description: Real PnL divided by theoretical PnL, after frictions; null if not measured.
realization_ratio.title: Realization Ratio

slippage_sens_delta.description: Change in realization_ratio when frictions are multiplied by 1.5; null if not measured.
slippage_sens_delta.title: Slippage Sens Delta

tools.name: registries
tools.description:
Requires the Stochastly desktop app: this tool runs inside the app, which is not installed on this machine. Install it from https://stochastly.com/pricing, open it and activate a licence.

List the strategy families, instrument groups and timeframes ("15M", "30M", "1H") the
app's built-in scanner screens are populated from, as `strategy_families`,
`instrument_groups` and `timeframes`.

For the node keys you pass to compose_graph or backtest_graph, use node_catalog instead;
for the cross-sectional crypto strategies, use crypto_registry. Needs Stochastly open with an
Atelier or Portfolio licence.

tools.name: research_status
tools.description:
Requires the Stochastly desktop app: this tool runs inside the app, which is not installed on this machine. Install it from https://stochastly.com/pricing, open it and activate a licence.

Read the saved journal of an in-app Research session: its status, turns, ideas, evidence,
token count and errors, with `age_s` since it was last saved.

Start a session with pilot_app(prompt="/research ...") and stop it with
pilot_app(prompt="/stop"). The journal is saved at start, after each turn and at the end,
so a `running` status is a checkpoint, not proof the session is still alive. Returns
`present: false` when no session exists. Needs Stochastly open with an Atelier or Portfolio
licence.

session_id.description: Journal id (lowercase letters, digits and dashes, no path or extension). Omit for the most recent session.
session_id.title: Session Id

tools.name: run_smoke_tests
tools.description:
Requires the Stochastly desktop app: this tool runs inside the app, which is not installed on this machine. Install it from https://stochastly.com/pricing, open it and activate a licence.

Development only: start the Playwright smoke test of the app interface (visual regression and
a clean console, headless, on mocked test data) and return pass or fail with the diagnostic line.

It needs a source checkout with its test harness installed. An installed app does not ship it,
so there the tool returns `dev_only: true` and starts nothing. Requires an Atelier or Portfolio
licence.

spec.description: Playwright spec file name inside the checkout's tests folder.
spec.title: Spec

timeout_s.description: Seconds before the test process tree is killed and a failure is returned.
timeout_s.title: Timeout S

tools.name: set_live_state
tools.description:
Requires the Stochastly desktop app: this tool runs inside the app, which is not installed on this machine. Install it from https://stochastly.com/pricing, open it and activate a licence.

Legacy: queue a command asking the old chart terminal to show another symbol or timeframe.
The current app does not apply these two fields, and the response says so.

To drive the current app (open a document, switch screen, start a backtest) use pilot_app.
The command replaces any pending one and only takes effect when piloting is enabled
(`pilot_enabled` in the response). Requires an Atelier or Portfolio licence.

sym.description: Symbol for the legacy chart terminal, for example "BTCUSDT".
sym.title: Sym

tf.description: Timeframe for the legacy chart terminal, for example "1h".
tf.title: Tf

annotations.title: Set symbol on the legacy chart

tools.name: tail_app_log
tools.description:
Requires the Stochastly desktop app: this tool runs inside the app, which is not installed on this machine. Install it from https://stochastly.com/pricing, open it and activate a licence.

Return the last lines of the app's own log file, with `present`, `age_s` and, when the log
is older than one hour, `stale: true` and a note saying it may describe an earlier session.

Use it to diagnose an app error. For a batch scanner run use v9_tail_log; for a graph run use
backtest_status. Needs Stochastly open with an Atelier or Portfolio licence.

lines.description: Number of trailing log lines to return.
lines.title: Lines

tools.name: v9_get_run
tools.description:
Requires the Stochastly desktop app: this tool runs inside the app, which is not installed on this machine. Install it from https://stochastly.com/pricing, open it and activate a licence.

Read one batch scanner run: its verdict file, the robustness counts (n_total,
n_robust_pass), its PBO and the last 30 log lines.

Use v9_list_runs first to find the run_id, and v9_tail_log for more log lines. Errors are
named: `no_runs` when nothing has run, `run_not_found` for an unknown id. Needs Stochastly
open with an Atelier or Portfolio licence.

run_id.description: A run_id from v9_list_runs, or "latest" for the newest run.
run_id.title: Run Id

tools.name: v9_list_runs
tools.description:
Requires the Stochastly desktop app: this tool runs inside the app, which is not installed on this machine. Install it from https://stochastly.com/pricing, open it and activate a licence.

List the runs of the separate batch strategy scanner (run folders named V9_* or V95_*),
newest first, each with run_id, status (running, done or error) and a summary (verdict,
n_configs, pbo_cscv, auc, best_config).

Use it to find a run_id for v9_get_run or v9_tail_log. Runs started from a graph are not
listed here: use backtest_status for those. Returns an empty list when the scanner is not
installed on this machine. Needs Stochastly open with an Atelier or Portfolio licence.

limit.description: Maximum number of runs returned, newest first.
limit.title: Limit

tools.name: v9_protocol_a
tools.description:
Requires the Stochastly desktop app: this tool runs inside the app, which is not installed on this machine. Install it from https://stochastly.com/pricing, open it and activate a licence.

Summarise the batch scanner's saved regression check: how many baseline configurations its
current engine reproduces from the previous one, as n_total, n_strict (exact matches), n_soft
(within tolerance), n_cumul, pct_cumul and the tolerance used.

It reads a result file computed earlier by the scanner and starts nothing. Returns the error
`no_protocol_a_results` when that file does not exist. Needs Stochastly open with an Atelier
or Portfolio licence.

tools.name: v9_tail_log
tools.description:
Requires the Stochastly desktop app: this tool runs inside the app, which is not installed on this machine. Install it from https://stochastly.com/pricing, open it and activate a licence.

Return the last lines of a batch scanner run's log file, as `lines`.

Use it to follow a running scan or see why one failed; v9_get_run gives the verdict and
robustness counts. An empty list means no run or no log yet. Needs Stochastly open with an
Atelier or Portfolio licence.

run_id.description: A run_id from v9_list_runs, or "latest" for the newest run.
run_id.title: Run Id

lines.description: Number of trailing log lines to return; must be 0 or more.
lines.title: Lines
